en: As long as I live, I won't sell this house.
es: Mientras viva, no venderé esta casa.
why: As long as, about the unknown future, takes the subjunctive.

en: As long as you have doubts, ask.
why: As long as, with an open time, takes the subjunctive.

en: We'll be fine as long as we stay together.
why: As long as, about the future, takes the subjunctive.

en: I'll wait as long as it's necessary.
why: As long as, about the future, takes the subjunctive.

en: As long as you don't tell me the truth, I won't help you.
es: Mientras no me digas la verdad, no te ayudo.
why: As long as, with a condition not yet met, takes the subjunctive.

en: As long as you pay, I'll cook.
why: As long as, with a condition, takes the subjunctive.

en: While Rosa was cooking, Tomás was setting the table.
es: Mientras Rosa cocinaba, Tomás ponía la mesa.
why: Two real actions at the same time take the indicative.

en: While I wash the dishes, you dry them.
es: Mientras yo lavo los platos, tú los secas.
why: Two actions happening together take the indicative.

en: Yesterday, while I was walking, I saw Don Hernando.
es: Ayer, mientras caminaba, vi a Don Hernando.
why: A real past moment takes the indicative.

en: While we eat, we watch the news.
why: A real habit at the same time takes the indicative.

en: While my mom was sleeping, I cleaned the house.
es: Mientras mi mamá dormía, yo limpié la casa.
why: A real past moment takes the indicative.

en: He talks on the phone while he drives.
why: Two real actions at the same time take the indicative.

en: While you were at work, someone called.
es: Mientras tú estabas en el trabajo, alguien llamó.
why: A real past moment takes the indicative.

en: While Simón studies, his sister plays.
es: Mientras Simón estudia, su hermana juega.
why: Two real actions at the same time take the indicative.
